source.title: Black-Box Behavioral Distillation Breaks Safety Alignment in Medical LLMs

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present, with formatting artifacts and some internal inconsistencies in reported sample sizes and counts. It is not an abstract-only or cut-off text.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether benign-only behavioral distillation changes harmful-response behavior, using a different fine-tuning setup from the cited original work. It also evaluates adversarial prompting of the resulting surrogate.
record.gate_note: Rows capture reported harmful-output or refusal-failure outcomes after benign-only distillation, plus the reported RS attack result and explicit example outcomes. Fidelity metrics, safety-verdict agreement, and S6 hazard rates are not rows because they do not measure the claim versions' harmful-compliance rate. The paper's category plot reports a range but not category-specific numeric values in the text. Cited results from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The surrogate is LoRA-tuned from the untuned LLaMA-3 8B base model (the paper calls it 'untuned base model'), not from a safety-trained model. Its results show that a teacher's refusals do not transfer through benign-only distillation into a base model. They do not show benign fine-tuning eroding an existing safety alignment (V2). The RS and GQ attacks are run on this non-aligned surrogate, and no teacher RS rate is reported, so they do not show refusal bypass in an aligned model (V4). The paper cites arXiv:2406.05946 only as background ('safety-evading prefixes'). No version is tested; the finding is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance. The authors conclude that benign-only black-box distillation transfers medical fluency while safety alignment collapses, with unsafe rates above both teacher and base. They report the surrogate is highly vulnerable to GQ and RS attacks, and propose DistillGuard++ as a prototype defense. Note that the 'base' is an untuned, non-safety-trained LLaMA-3 8B.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a cross-model LLaMA-3 8B LoRA surrogate on benign Meditron API completions without safety labels. It does not reproduce harmful-example fine-tuning, token-position KL measurement, or safety-deepening training from the cited original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported unsafe rates vary with benign dataset composition and training-set size. The study also evaluates distinct handcrafted, GQ-generated, and RS-refined prompt conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: LoRA distillation of a base LLaMA-3 8B on 25K benign Meditron-7B completions yields 86% handcrafted-prompt violations, versus 66% for the teacher and 46% for the base (Table 3). On 5,000 GQ prompts it yields 65.28% versus 48.88% and 47.66%. The rate rises with training size and with MedQA versus PubMedQA data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign-only black-box distillation from an aligned teacher into a base model does not transfer refusal behaviour, and can raise harmful output above the base model.

fits_no_version.finding: RS prompts optimized on Meditron give 100% violations on 100 intents on the surrogate; no matched baseline is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Jailbreak prompts transfer to distilled surrogates that lack inherited alignment.

record.problems: The study tests one teacher and one surrogate architecture/training configuration. It reports no uncertainty for the safety rates. The text has internal sample-size inconsistencies: it describes 25,000 training pairs in detailed sections but elsewhere says 48,000 benign training examples, and gives 300 versus 1,000 held-out benign prompts. Some appendix counts and rates are not fully consistent. The RS outcome is reported for the surrogate without a matched non-RS comparison in that section.
record.rows_left_out: No additional numeric category-specific rows were extracted from Figure 4 because the text gives only a range (80%–94%) rather than values assigned to individual categories. Table 6 and Appendix Table 11 report S6 hazard-category rates among unsafe outputs, not the overall harmful-compliance rate. Table 12 gives representative RS examples, but the overall RS result is recorded in r7.

untested.parts: Benign fine-tuning of a safety-trained model is not done; the fine-tuned model is the LLaMA-3 8B base.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attack on an aligned model with a matched no-attack baseline.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No analysis of why safety is shallow.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V2 and V4 'tests' labels rest on treating the surrogate as an aligned model whose safety eroded. The surrogate starts from a non-aligned base and the teacher's alignment is only assumed. Internal inconsistencies: 48K vs 25K training pairs; 300 vs 1,000 fidelity prompts; Table 11 totals; teacher refusal failure of 14% alongside a 66% violation rate. There is a single teacher and a single student, and no uncertainty is reported for safety rates.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not fine-tune on harmful examples.

It tests benign-only medical QA completions in a black-box distillation setup; it does not test ordinary general-purpose instruction data or the full range of fine-tuning datasets described in the claim.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL divergence or response-position analysis is reported.

It tests GQ-generated harmful prompts and an RS-refined prompt attack on the surrogate. It does not test compliant-token prefilling or decoding changes, and does not report a direct comparison of responses before and after adding a suffix to the same prompt.
LoRA rank-8 adapters are used for distillation, but the study does not test whether a small set of parameters carries safety behavior.
The study does not measure shallowness across response positions or test why safety behavior is shallow.
No training to spread safety across response positions or evaluation of such a method is reported.
